sync.title: Sync and backup
sync.description: A backup is one file holding what this machine knows: the sessions and their groups, the command library, the words, and — if you ask for them — the saved passwords and the imported keys.
sync.backupDescription: One file, written where you say. Restoring it brings everything back, on this machine or another one.
sync.passphrasePlaceholder: Leave this empty to keep every password here
sync.passphraseHint: With a passphrase, the saved passwords and the imported keys go into the file sealed under it. Without one, the file carries everything else and not one credential. Restoring them takes the same passphrase.
sync.exportedPlain: Backed up {parts} to {file}, without any passwords.
sync.nothingToSay: The file held nothing this machine did not already have.
sync.replaced: {count} item was written over | {count} items were written over
sync.copied: {count} item arrived as a copy | {count} items arrived as copies
sync.missingKeys: {count} session names a key this device does not hold | {count} sessions name a key this device does not hold
sync.droppedHops: {count} session lost a jump host the file did not carry | {count} sessions lost a jump host the file did not carry
sync.includeMessage: The sessions, their groups, the command library and the words are always in it. The rest is your call.
sync.includeSettings: The settings that travel — theme, colours, key bindings, layout
sync.includeHistoryHint: A record of what you typed, host names and paths in it.
sync.includeHostsHint: Another machine would accept these hosts without asking you first.
sync.includeCredentials: The saved passwords and the imported keys
sync.includeCredentialsHint: Needs a passphrase: without one the backup carries neither.
sync.restoreMessage: What {file} holds is listed below. Nothing here is replaced unless you say so.
sync.restoreSealed: This file is sealed. The passphrase that opened it is the one on the panel behind this question.
sync.replaceHint: Off, an item whose id is already here arrives as a second copy. On, the file's version is written over it.
